subject: China
note: Cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary): Time in China. Xinjiang is described as the page does: two time standards used in parallel.

claims.text: China follows a single standard time offset of UTC+08:00 (Beijing Time), even though the country spans five geographical time zones.
It is the largest sovereign nation in the world that officially observes only one time zone.
In Xinjiang, two time standards are used in parallel, Beijing Time and Xinjiang Time (UTC+06:00), which is two hours behind Beijing.
Stores and offices in Xinjiang are commonly open from 10:00 to 19:00 Beijing Time, which equals 08:00 to 17:00 in Ürümqi Time.
At the Wakhjir Pass the clocks change from UTC+08:00 in China to UTC+04:30 in Afghanistan, the biggest official change at any land frontier.
